title: Label fusion and training methods for reliable representation of inter-rater uncertainty
mechanism: Compares STAPLE, averaging and random per-iteration rater sampling of multi-rater labels, combined with SoftSeg (regression on soft labels). The result is better calibration with equal or better Dice.
adaptation: Where a cell has two crack label versions (2021 vs 2022, or E-SCDD re-annotations), train crack on soft averaged labels or a random version per iteration. Score on revised labels and on the union.
min_experiment: Arm: house with soft or random-version crack targets. Baseline: house on revised labels. Metric: clean-49 relF1@2 and crack IoU. Kill: relF1@2 more than 0.005 below the baseline. First count the train cells with two independent versions.
prior_overlap: none: soft-label losses and annotator modelling are listed as open in BRIEF section 5.
evidence: R: 10 splits on 2 public multi-rater datasets (spinal cord gray matter, MS lesions). SoftSeg is equal or better in Dice and better calibrated; the best fusion method was task-dependent.
